AVAIF: CORRECTED from PASS. AVA Infrastructure Fund's core business activities focus on providing debt financing for infrastructure development projects across Nigeria (greenfield developments, expansion, recapitalisations, rehabilitation of mature assets). Its own stated objective is to deliver income to unit holders through debt financing, with management describing its strategy as allocating private credit. Same category as NIDF, CNIF, and MOFIREIF - a debt fund, not a property-holding trust, despite the infrastructure/real estate framing.
AVACAP: CORRECTED from REVIEW. United Capital Plc directly operates UCEE Microfinance Bank as a named core segment, plus a Consumer Finance segment engaged in consumer lending and MSME financing - not incidental interest income, but directly operated lending subsidiaries. Clean fee-based lines (asset management, stockbroking, advisory, trusteeship) exist alongside this, but same pattern as VFD Group: a directly operated bank/lending arm as a core segment is not offset by other clean segments.
CHAMPION: CORRECTED from original PASS/VERIFY classification. Champion Breweries Plc is a straightforward alcohol producer - brews and markets Champion Lager Beer and other alcoholic beverages as core, majority-revenue products; Heineken International holds a majority equity stake since 2014. Same category as NB, Guinness, and International Breweries.
CMFC: CORRECTED - this is NOT Consolidated Hallmark Insurance as originally misidentified. CMFC is Critical Minerals Financing Corp Plc, formerly Deap Capital Management & Trust Plc (DEAPCAP), rebranded June 2026 into a specialised mining, metals, commodities finance and investment platform - capital structuring, investment banking, transaction advisory, project development support, and financing solutions for the minerals/commodities sector. No line-item CMFC revenue disclosure confirms this, but per typical revenue patterns of comparable mining/commodities financing corporations, 'financing solutions' and 'capital structuring' in this space are overwhelmingly monetized through structured debt and interest spread rather than fee-only advisory (the same pattern confirmed directly for UCAP once its lending subsidiary was examined) - treated as FAIL on that basis.
CNIF: CORRECTED from PASS. Coronation Infrastructure Fund is explicitly a closed-end debt fund, investing in loans, securities and securitised debt instruments of infrastructure companies, targeting a return of 3% over the FGN bond yield. H1 2026 results confirm interest income as the Fund's primary revenue driver, with infrastructure loans and money-market placements as the main contributors. Same category as NIDF and MOFIREIF - interest-based lending as the core, explicit product, not a property-holding trust.

Also carries elevated financial risk: FY2025 revenue of ~N67-147m against a loss after tax of N1.596bn, and a recent N6.3bn debt-to-equity conversion signaling heavy prior leverage.

MOFIREIF: CORRECTED from original PASS classification, which mistakenly treated this as a property-holding REIT. MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF) is actually a government-backed mortgage lending vehicle, not a rental-property trust - its core business is originating fixed-rate mortgage loans to homebuyers at a stated 9.75% interest rate (well below commercial bank rates of 18-22%), plus construction financing guarantees to developers, with repayments recycled into new loans. Interest-bearing lending is the core product, not an incidental tenant-mix issue like genuine property REITs (NREIT, UPDCREIT, SFSREIT, UHOMREIT) - same category as the mortgage banks (INFINITY, LIVINGTRUST) already marked FAIL.

NIDF: CORRECTED from original PASS/VERIFY classification. Nigeria Infrastructure Debt Fund is explicitly a debt fund, not a property-holding trust - it makes primarily debt investments in infrastructure projects, targeting a gross return of 3.00-4.50% over comparable FGN bond yields, with 80% of assets in senior debt/securitised debt/loans to government agencies. Income to unit-holders comes from coupon and fees received from borrowers. This is interest-based lending as the core, explicit product (not incidental), same category as MOFIREIF, INFINITY, and LIVINGTRUST.
NSLTECH: CORRECTED from original PASS classification, which was in error. Secure Electronic Technology Plc (formerly National Sports Lottery Plc) directly operates a licensed national lottery business in Nigeria (exclusive 15-year license from Dec 2001), with stated operations covering lottery business, gaming products, airtime vending, and card payments. FY2025 financials show prize/winnings costs of N2.32bn and ticket costs of N1.60bn - core revenue is lottery/gambling activity, not incidental.

ZICHIS: Core activities (oil palm, poultry, fish farming, feed milling, crop cultivation, snail farming) are permissible, but the company's own NGX listing announcement names piggery among its stated business lines - swine farming is a categorical exclusion regardless of revenue share. Current public-facing materials (company site, most profiles) omit piggery, so current materiality is unconfirmed - needs direct segment-revenue check in latest annual report/prospectus. Separately, NGX suspended trading and opened an investigation into the stock after an 859% one-month price surge - a governance/integrity risk independent of the halal screen.
VETGRIF30: Vetiva Griffin 30 ETF - tracks the NGX 30 Index, which holds conventional (interest-based) banks (Zenith Bank, GTCO, UBA, etc.) and other companies that fail the business-activity screen directly as portfolio constituents; a Shariah-compliant investor cannot look through to only the permissible names inside a passively-replicated index fund.
STANBICETF30: Stanbic IBTC ETF 30 - tracks the same NGX 30 Index as VETGRIF30, so it directly holds conventional banks and other impermissible constituents as core portfolio holdings.
VETBANK: Vetiva Banking ETF - tracks the NGX Banking Index, i.e. a basket of the top 10 conventional (interest-based) banks listed on NGX; a dedicated sector fund investing exclusively in an impermissible activity.
GREENWETF: Greenwich Alpha ETF - tracks the broad NGX All-Share Index, which includes conventional banks, insurers, breweries and other impermissible names as core constituents alongside permissible companies; a market-cap-weighted all-share tracker cannot exclude these holdings.
VSPBONDETF: Vetiva S&P Nigeria Sovereign Bond ETF - holds a basket of Federal Government of Nigeria bonds and generates its return from fixed coupon (interest) income; a conventional fixed-income instrument, which is riba by definition.
SIAMLETF40: SIAML Pension ETF 40 - tracks the NGX Pension Index (top 40 pension-fund-eligible companies across all sectors), which includes conventional banks and insurers as core constituents; a broad-based tracker cannot exclude these impermissible holdings.
